exposure: type of embryo transfer (fresh embryo transfer vs. frozen embryo transfer)
cohort: The study included 25,863 singletons born after either fresh or frozen embryo transfer.
finding: Full-term singletons born after frozen embryo transfer (FET) had a higher birthweight, a higher risk of large for gestational age (LGA), and a lower risk of small for gestational age (SGA) compared to those born after fresh embryo transfer (Fre-ET), while no such differences were observed in preterm singletons.
birth_weight: Birthweight was measured in singletons, with specific means for full-term infants born after FET (3497.58 ± 439.73 g) and Fre-ET (3445.67 ± 450.24 g) provided.
gest_age: All gestational ages for singletons, with specific analysis focusing on differences observed at 37 gestational weeks or later (full-term) but not in preterm singletons.
